questions.q: According to this capstone, what did Chapter 1 actually teach, and why did it matter to Lesson 29's script?
options: The two questions to answer before writing any script — the right tool for the job, and whether it's safe to rerun — which Lesson 29 answered with PowerShell and a power-state check
The specific syntax for Stop-AzVM and Start-AzVM
How to install the Az PowerShell module
A list of every Azure resource type that can be automated
questions.explain: Chapter 1 taught tool choice, idempotency, and error handling as foundational questions, which Lesson 29's script put into practice directly.

questions.q: Why did Lesson 30's compliance script use Python instead of PowerShell, according to this review?
options: A tag check across every resource type benefits from Python's general-purpose data handling more than it needs PowerShell's Azure-specific cmdlet shape
PowerShell cannot connect to Azure at all
Python is always the correct choice over PowerShell for any Azure task
The script needed to run on a Linux-only pipeline, which PowerShell cannot do
questions.explain: The lesson frames tool choice as job-dependent: Lesson 29 picked PowerShell for an Azure-native task, Lesson 30 picked Python for general-purpose data handling across resource types.

questions.q: How does this lesson distinguish Chapter 5's Infrastructure as Code previews from the operational automation in Chapters 1-4 and 6?
options: IaC declares what infrastructure should exist and previews it before creation, while operational automation manages infrastructure that already exists
They are the same thing, just using different tools
IaC is only used for deleting resources, never creating them
Operational automation always runs before IaC in a deployment
questions.explain: The review explicitly separates the two: IaC previews answer 'what should exist,' while this chapter's scripts answer 'how do we operate what already exists.'

questions.q: What three Chapter 7 practices does this review credit with turning Lesson 30's script into something that could catch Lesson 31's near-miss?
options: Source control, running from a pipeline instead of a laptop, and pipeline-managed secrets
Faster hardware, better naming conventions, and more frequent backups
Manual testing, weekly stand-up meetings, and code comments
Using Python exclusively, disabling the portal, and removing all tags
questions.explain: This matches Lesson 31's case study directly: source control, pipeline execution, and pipeline-handled secrets are what made the nightly check trustworthy.

questions.q: What course comes next in this path after this course completes the Job-Ready Foundation stage's automation content?
options: Cloud Deployment, Monitoring, Backup & Job-Ready Capstone
Advanced Terraform and Bicep
Kafka and Event Streaming
Azure Fundamentals
questions.explain: The course-complete outro names Cloud Deployment, Monitoring, Backup & Job-Ready Capstone as the next course, which closes the Job-Ready Foundation stage.
